Each entry is the coded remedy kind / 根拠法令 (statutory or scheme basis) / statutory window (日数, where one exists) / 書面 form / delivery channel / escalation forum so kurashimori can diagnose + (eventually) help draft procedurally. CRITICAL: statutory cooling-off / withdrawal windows (日数) drift and vary by transaction type and jurisdiction — a wrong 日数 is harmful; these are best-effort references as of 2026-06-02 and MUST be verified against the cited official source before any live use. Boundary holds in every jurisdiction — 弁護士法 / 司法書士法 / UPL (and national analogs: German RDG, French monopole de l'avocat, Advocates Act 1961, Legal Profession Act, Law Society Act): self-help diagnosis + drafting-assist only. targets.title: FTC Cooling-Off Rule — 3-day right to cancel home/off-premises sales (Cooling-Off Rule / 訪問販売クーリングオフ)
targets.windowStart: Midnight of the 3rd BUSINESS DAY after the qualifying sale (business days only; many exclusions)
targets.deliveryChannel: Written cancellation notice to the seller within the window
targets.escalationForum: U.S. Federal Trade Commission complaint portal https://reportfraud.ftc.gov
targets.legalBasis: FTC Trade Regulation Rule Concerning Cooling-Off Period for Sales Made at Homes or at Certain Other Locations, 16 CFR Part 429 (esp. § 429.1)
targets.notes: Authority: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Bureau of Consumer Protection. Consumer guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/buyers-remorse-ftcs-cooling-rule-may-help. Gives buyer until midnight of the 3rd BUSINESS DAY to cancel certain sales of $25+ made at home/workplace/dorm or seller's temporary location (hotel, fairground, etc.). Counting business days is arithmetic, NOT a legal opinion on whether a given sale qualifies (many exclusions: real estate, insurance, sales made entirely by mail/phone, under $25, at seller's permanent place of business). Drift: dollar threshold and covered-location definitions have been amended over time; confirm current text on eCFR before relying. Cooling-off windows are INFORMATIONAL date computation, NOT a legal opinion. No representation, no claims-buying, no fees.

targets.title: FTC Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule — 30-day shipment / prompt-refund (Mail Order Rule / 通信販売発送・返金ルール)
targets.windowStart: Seller must ship within the advertised time or, if none stated, within 30 days; refund within 7 working days once the right vests (or one billing cycle for credit-card sales)
targets.deliveryChannel: Demand letter to the seller
targets.escalationForum: U.S. Federal Trade Commission complaint portal https://reportfraud.ftc.gov
targets.legalBasis: Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule, 16 CFR Part 435 (esp. § 435.2)
targets.notes: Authority: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Bureau of Consumer Protection. Rule text: https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/rules/mail-internet-or-telephone-order-merchandise-rule. For mail/internet/phone orders, seller must ship within the advertised time or, if none stated, within 30 days; otherwise must obtain buyer consent to delay or issue a prompt refund (refund within 7 working days once the right vests, or one billing cycle for credit-card sales). NOTE: this is a distance-selling SHIPMENT/refund rule — it is NOT a general 'change of mind' return right; US has no blanket federal distance-selling withdrawal window like the EU. Retailer return policies are contractual, not statutory. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing/wayfinding only. 弁護士法 / 司法書士法 / UPL: self-help diagnosis + drafting-assist only. targets.title: Fair Credit Billing Act — credit-card billing-error dispute / chargeback (FCBA / クレジット請求エラー異議)
targets.windowStart: Issuer must RECEIVE the written billing-error notice within 60 days after the first statement showing the error
targets.deliveryChannel: Written billing-error notice mailed to card issuer's billing-inquiries address
targets.escalationForum: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/
targets.legalBasis: Fair Credit Billing Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 1666–1666j (Truth in Lending Act amendment); implemented by Regulation Z, 12 CFR § 1026.13
targets.notes: Authority: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) — implementing Regulation Z; card issuer handles the dispute. For OPEN-END credit (credit cards): mail a written billing-error notice so the issuer RECEIVES it within 60 days after the first statement showing the error. Issuer must acknowledge within 30 days and resolve within two billing cycles (max 90 days); disputed amount need not be paid and credit rating cannot be threatened during investigation. Separate from network 'chargeback' timelines (Visa/Mastercard rules) and from debit-card disputes (those fall under EFTA/Reg E, different deadlines). The 60-day window is INFORMATIONAL arithmetic, NOT legal advice on whether an item is a qualifying 'billing error.' targets.title: Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act — federal consumer-product warranty enforcement (MMWA / 連邦保証法)
targets.windowStart: (per the written warranty's stated term; no statutory fixed window)
targets.deliveryChannel: Warrantor's stated informal dispute-settlement (IDS) process / demand submission
targets.escalationForum: Warrantor IDS (mediation/arbitration); courts for private enforcement
targets.legalBasis: Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 2301–2312; FTC IDS rule 16 CFR Part 703
targets.notes: Authority: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) — rulemaking/enforcement; private enforcement via courts and warrantor informal dispute settlement (IDS). Statute index: https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/statutes/magnuson-moss-warranty-federal-trade-commission-improvements-act. Governs written warranties on consumer products costing more than the regulatory threshold; requires clear disclosure and lets consumers use the warrantor's informal dispute-settlement (mediation/arbitration) procedure and, where applicable, sue (attorney-fee shifting possible). Does NOT require a product to carry a warranty. A 'full' vs 'limited' warranty designation has specific statutory meaning. Drift: dollar thresholds in FTC rules; many disputes overlap with state lemon/warranty law (see CA entry). targets.title: EU 14-day right of withdrawal for distance & off-premises contracts (Right of withdrawal / Widerrufsrecht / Droit de rétractation)
targets.windowStart: 14 calendar days: for goods, from physical possession; for services, from contract conclusion (Art. 9); +12 months if trader failed to inform (Art. 10)
targets.deliveryChannel: Withdrawal notice to trader (Annex I(B) model form or any unequivocal statement)
targets.escalationForum: National consumer authority / national ADR body / ECC-Net for cross-border
targets.legalBasis: Directive 2011/83/EU on Consumer Rights (Consumer Rights Directive), Articles 9–16 (esp. Art. 9 = 14-day period; Art. 11 = exercise; Art. 13–14 = refund/return; Art. 10 = 12-month extension if trader failed to inform; Art. 16 = exceptions)
targets.notes: Authority: European Commission, DG Justice and Consumers (transposed and enforced by each Member State's consumer authority). Guide: https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/consumer-protection-law/consumer-contract-law/consumer-rights-directive_en. Window is 14 calendar days: for goods, from the day the consumer/third party acquires physical possession; for services, from contract conclusion (Art. 9). If the trader never disclosed the withdrawal right, the period extends by up to 12 months (Art. 10). Key exceptions in Art. 16: custom/personalised goods, sealed health/hygiene goods once unsealed, perishables, dated accommodation/transport, fully-performed services the consumer expressly requested. A real deadline turns on disclosure facts and exception triggers we cannot adjudicate. DRIFT WARNING: Directive (EU) 2023/2673 adds a mandatory 'cancel my contract' withdrawal function from ~June 2026; verify the as-applicable national transposition. targets.title: EU minimum 2-year legal guarantee of conformity (repair/replace/refund) (Legal guarantee / Gewährleistung / Garantie légale de conformité)

targets.deliveryChannel: Claim asserted directly to the seller (not the manufacturer)
targets.escalationForum: National consumer authority / national ADR body / ECC-Net for cross-border
targets.legalBasis: Directive (EU) 2019/771 on contracts for the sale of goods, Articles 10–14 (Art. 10 = liability for non-conformity apparent within ≥2 years; Art. 11 = burden-of-proof reversal for first ≥1 year; Art. 13–14 = hierarchy of remedies: repair/replacement then price reduction/termination). Repealed Directive 1999/44/EC; applies from 1 Jan 2022.
targets.notes: Authority: European Commission, DG Justice and Consumers (transposed into national civil/consumer codes; enforced per Member State). Guide: https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/consumer-protection-law/consumer-contract-law/consumer-sales-and-guarantees_en. Distinct from the voluntary commercial warranty (Art. 17): the legal guarantee is mandatory and free. Seller liable for defects present at delivery that appear within at least 2 years; during at least the first year the defect is presumed pre-existing (seller bears burden). Member States may set longer periods (e.g., France's presomption runs 24 months; some states allow longer guarantee terms) — verify the specific national transposition before relying on a deadline. Conformity, the remedy hierarchy and time-limits are fact-specific. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold — not for live use. 弁護士法 / 司法書士法 / UPL: self-help diagnosis + drafting-assist only.
